content:
The Time & Work chapter is a high-yield part of the CAT Quantitative Aptitude section, and a favourite in XAT, SNAP, NMAT and CMAT too. This guide explains what CAT Time & Work tests, the formulas and shortcuts worth memorising, the mistakes that cost marks, and a free 10-question online test you can take right now.

Take the quiz below first, read the explanation for anything you miss, then use the chapter e-book at the end for full, exam-level practice.

What CAT asks on Time & Work

Work rates, combined work, efficiency comparison, pipes and cisterns, and wages in proportion to work done.

Key formulas & shortcuts

  • If A finishes in a days, A’s one-day work = 1/a.
  • Together A and B take ab/(a+b) days.
  • Work ∝ men × days × hours (chain rule M₁D₁H₁/W₁ = M₂D₂H₂/W₂).
  • Wages are shared in the ratio of work done.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Adding days instead of adding rates (1/a + 1/b).
  • Ignoring an outlet pipe when computing net fill.
  • Not accounting for different efficiencies.

quiz.title: CAT Time & Work Practice Quiz
quiz.intro: Ten CAT-pattern questions. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.

questions.q: If 6 men or 8 women can complete a piece of work in 24 days, in how many days can 9 men and 12 women working together complete the same work?
questions.explanation:
1. Equating total work: 6M * 24 = 8W * 24 =  6M = 8W => 3M = 4W.
2. Total work in terms of men = 6 * 24 = 144 man-days.
3. We need work done by (9M + 12W).
4. Convert 12W into equivalent men: Since 4W = 3M, 12W = 3 * 3M = 9M.
5. Total workforce = 9M + 9M = 18M.
6. Days required = Total work / Total workforce = 144 / 18

questions.q: A and B together can do a piece of work in 12 days. B alone can do it in 30 days. In how many days can A alone finish the work?
questions.explanation:
1. Let total work = LCM(12, 30) = 60 units.
2. Combined efficiency (A + B) = 60 / 12 = 5 units/day.
3. B's efficiency = 60 / 30 = 2 units/day.
4. A's efficiency = (A + B) - B = 5 - 2 = 3 units/day.
5. Time taken by A alone = 60 / 3 = 20 days.

faq.a: Rates are additive (work per day); days are not. Together their rate is 1/a + 1/b, so time = ab/(a+b).

faq.q: How are pipes and cisterns handled?
faq.a: Inlets add +1/a, outlets subtract −1/b; the net rate fills (or empties) the tank.
